Salesforce Stocks Fall 9.45% in Worst Day Since 2024 as AI Agents Rattle Software

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Salesforce (NYSE:CRM) tumbled 9.45% to $194.52 at the 4:00 p.m. ET close on November 17, its worst session since May 2024, as investors sold software names exposed to AI agents. Peers ServiceNow and Intuit each lost more than 6%, and the selloff landed two days before Anthropic's planned Nasdaq debut.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 8 Warning Signs with JPM.

Is CRM fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

CRM GF Value chart

The trigger was a new model, not a Salesforce headline. OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra the same day at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, and SiliconANGLE reported that it was trained to build slides, spreadsheets and documents for law, sales, finance and accounting. Salesforce's own numbers remain solid: Agentforce annual recurring revenue tops $1.5 billion, combined Agentforce and Data 360 ARR is near $3.9 billion, current remaining performance obligation rose 14% to $33.5 billion, and fiscal 2027 revenue guidance sits at $46.1 billion to $46.4 billion.

That $3.9 billion equals only about 8.4% of guided revenue, so most of the business still runs on seats that AI agents could shrink. At roughly 17.7 times earnings and a $160 billion market value, the market is pricing that risk aggressively. GuruFocus scores Salesforce 88/100, reflecting strong profitability and a mid-range balance sheet. Its GF Value of $359.30 implies the shares trade about 46% below the model, which GuruFocus labels significantly undervalued, but a model anchored to past growth cannot capture a structural shift in seat counts. The next hurdle is the December 2 report, where cRPO and Agentforce growth must show agents adding revenue faster than they erode licenses.

Is Salesforce's AI Sell-Off A Cash Bargain?
Trefis Team

Today's big story: Anthropic IPO: Priced For 2031, Or 2036?

Salesforce stock fell 9.5% on Tuesday, Nov 17, to close at $194.52. It was the stock's largest one-day fall since May 30, 2024, when it dropped 19.7%. The S&P 500 lost 1.0% the same day. ServiceNow fell 6.5% and Adobe fell 4.2%.

Why did it fall? MarketWatch reported that a series of technology outages left investors worried that software companies could be "particularly vulnerable" to AI misuse, citing an analyst. Invezz tied the fall to the same outages and to worries about software reliability and security. The Motley Fool said security jitters and fears that AI could replace software hit the whole group. Business Insider reported the same day that Salesforce has started cutting more jobs. No outlet showed that the job cuts moved the stock.

Most coverage focuses on the fear that AI could replace software. This article looks at cash. At Tuesday's close, Salesforce traded at 10.5 times the free cash it produced over the past year. Free cash flow is the cash left after running the business and paying for equipment. Measured the same way at each quarter end since 2010, only two readings were lower. So the stock is near its cheapest on cash in that record, but this is not a record low.

How Cheap Is Salesforce On Cash?

The price of 10.5 times cash flow equals a free cash flow yield of 9.5%. Across 67 quarter ends since 2010, the middle reading was 40.2 times. The lowest was just under 10 times, at the end of July 2026.

The stock got cheap quickly. It traded at 19.2 times cash flow at the end of October 2025. That fell to 13.8 times by the end of January 2026 and to 10.5 times by the end of April, a touch below Tuesday's reading. The shares are down 26.6% this year. They closed 27.4% below their 52-week high and 47.1% below their record close of $367.87 on Dec 4, 2024. Tuesday's close was the lowest since Aug 17.

One peer is cheaper than Salesforce on this measure and one is more expensive. Here is the same measure for the two software stocks that fell with it.

On this measure Salesforce is far cheaper than ServiceNow. Adobe is cheaper still, at 8.8 times. We looked at the same question for ServiceNow in how ServiceNow's cash yield compares with Treasury bonds.

The Business Behind The Price

The low price is not because cash is shrinking. Free cash flow over the year to July 2026 was $15,154 million. That is 21.3% more than a year earlier. Revenue in the three months to July grew 10.8% from a year before.

title: Okta vs. SentinelOne: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

Okta vs. SentinelOne: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

As digital threats grow more sophisticated, enterprises are prioritizing identity management and endpoint security to protect their networks. Choosing between Okta (NASDAQ:OKTA)and SentinelOne (NYSE:S)requires weighing established profitability against rapid growth.

Okta focuses on securing identities, ensuring only authorized users can access sensitive data across cloud applications. SentinelOne uses artificial intelligence to detect and respond to threats across devices and cloud workloads. Both companies are essential players in the tech stocks landscape, providing critical infrastructure for a cloud-first world.

The case for Okta

Okta provides a cloud-based platform that manages and secures identities for both workers and customers. The company serves over 20,000 organizations, ranging from small businesses to large government agencies and universities. Its ecosystem includes the Okta Integration Network, which features over 7,000 pre-built integrations with providers like Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT), Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), and Salesforce (NYSE:CRM).

In the 12 months ended July 31, 2026, revenue reached nearly $3.1 billion. This figure represents revenue growth of approximately 11.2% compared to the prior twelve-month period. For that same time frame, the company reported net income of roughly $296.0 million, reflecting its position as an established player in its industry.

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was nearly 0.1x, a measure of total debt relative to shareholders' equity. The current ratio, which indicates the ability to pay short-term obligations using short-term assets, was approximately 1.4x. In the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, free cash flow was nearly $863.0 million, though note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 61.5% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation.

The case for SentinelOne

SentinelOne offers the Singularity platform, an AI-powered solution that protects endpoints, cloud workloads, and network-connected devices. The company relies on an extensive network of channel partners to fulfill sales, including resellers and distributors. Recently, it expanded its footprint through partnerships with firms such as N-able (NYSE:NABL)and Lenovo to integrate security directly into enterprise devices.

In the 12 months ended July 31, 2026, revenue reached nearly $1.1 billion. This was driven by revenue growth of approximately 21.1% over the preceding twelve months. Despite this top-line expansion, the company reported a net loss of roughly $340.1 million for the period as it continues to prioritize market share gains.

RBC Analyst Warns AI Companies Will "Try to Destroy Salesforce Entirely." And It Can't Lock Them Out ©@Blue Planet Studio from Getty Images via Canva, @Blue Planet Studio from Getty Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

RBC analyst Rishi Jaluria said Salesforce can't shut off its customers' access to whatever AI model they want, with Anthropic's IPO expected this week.

That lets AI labs compete for the work and the per-seat pricing behind Salesforce's growth plan, a pressure ServiceNow faces too.

Analysts still expect Salesforce's revenue to grow from $41.5 billion to $55.7 billion over three fiscal years.

At 15x forward earnings, about half its five-year average, the stock already prices in much of that threat, and the Dec. 2 report is the next test.

Salesforce (CRM:NYSE) can't keep its customers' data away from the AI models they choose. With Anthropic's IPO expected this week, that matters more than it sounds.

Rishi Jaluria, a software analyst at RBC Capital Markets, talked about it on this week's episode of the RiskReversal Pod. Asked whether partnerships with the frontier labs could put a floor under software stocks, he said the ones on display at Salesforce's Dreamforce conference start "to put a little bit of a damper in the, hey, you know, the AI companies are going to try to destroy Salesforce entirely, right?"

Then he made the point that matters more for shareholders:

"You can't say we're going to shut off Salesforce access to whatever AI model that our customers want to use. We have to have that integration."

For the labs, that's an open invitation.

TIKR tracks 56 analysts on Salesforce. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Salesforce, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Salesforce's Analyst Ratings

Salesforce left the door open on purpose

Any customer that can point Claude at its Salesforce data now gets to choose where the work happens. And that customer is still looking for a payoff from what it's already spent. Jaluria said enterprises are "still debating, okay, we've spent all this money, where are we getting the cost savings that are tangible in metrics?" A customer asking that, with its data a click away from Claude, has every reason to push back on paying for seats an agent is starting to fill.

Salesforce isn't alone here. ServiceNow (NOW:NYSE) runs IT workflows I'd expect the labs to want to build on too. And Salesforce is going after ServiceNow directly: more than 450 customers use its IT service management product, including some that switched over from ServiceNow, it said on its second-quarter call.

Key Takeaways

BTIG cut its Salesforce price target to $250 from $300 on Nov. 18 and kept its Buy rating, so the target is still 33% above the share price.

Salesforce fell 9% on Nov. 17 after tech outages and a data breach hit software stocks ahead of Anthropic's IPO, adding to a year of worries about growth, debt and AI.

At $250, Salesforce would trade at about 14x the earnings analysts expect for the year ending January 2029, close to its multiple today and about half its five-year average.

BTIG's lower target looks too cautious, and the third-quarter report on Dec. 2 will show whether organic growth is picking up.

Salesforce (CRM:NYSE) sits 30% below its December high, and one of its bulls just lowered the bar. BTIG cut its price target to $250 from $300 on Nov. 18 and kept its Buy rating. That's still 33% above today's $188.

Slow growth, more debt and a rough week

Salesforce's revenue rose 11% to $11.3 billion in its second quarter, ended July 31, but $456 million of that came from Informatica. Without it, revenue grew 6%. Chief Financial and Operating Officer Robin Washington said the company is "on track for second-half organic revenue reacceleration."

Salesforce's debt rose to $39.5 billion by July 31, from $14.5 billion at the end of January, to pay for a $25 billion buyback. S&P cut its credit rating to A from A+ on Nov. 4, citing the deals and shareholder returns.

On Nov. 17, the stock fell 9% as a run of tech outages and a data breach at Optimizely that named Salesforce hit software stocks ahead of Anthropic's IPO.

Salesforce (NYSE:CRM) has begun another round of job cuts, Business Insider reported, citing internal employee communications. The scope of the layoffs remains unclear.

Salesforce shares fell 9.45% to $194.52 on Tuesday as investors weighed how AI could reshape demand for traditional enterprise software.

Employees discussed recent departures in an internal Slack channel, according to the report. A senior manager working in IT compliance and content strategy also said in a public LinkedIn post that they and several teammates were affected on Monday.

The latest cuts follow earlier reductions, including 86 jobs in California in August across sales, administration, and technology and product roles, according to a regulatory filing cited in the report.

Separately, Salesforce set budgets for employee AI usage after some workers incurred thousands of dollars in AI token costs during the previous quarter, Business Insider reported. The company is also pursuing its $5.66 billion acquisition of Braze, a customer engagement platform that Salesforce plans to combine with its marketing and data tools.

Investors Takeaway

Salesforce reports earnings after the bell on Dec. 2. Any update on the scale of the layoffs would help investors gauge their effect on operating expenses. The broader test is whether customers are paying for Agentforce and other AI products at a pace that can meaningfully lift revenue.

That will be easier to judge if management breaks out paid adoption and explains how it is affecting spending on Salesforce's existing software.
